title: AGMark: Attention-Guided Dynamic Watermarking for Large Vision-Language Models

problem.claim: Watermarking for large vision-language models must support content traceability and intellectual property protection while preserving visual-semantic fidelity.

gap.claim: Existing vision-agnostic and vision-specific watermarks can disrupt visual grounding, use static estimates of vision-critical weights, ignore weight distribution density, and introduce low-quality or irrelevant tokens.

contributions.claim: AGMark dynamically identifies semantic-critical evidence using attention-based visual relevance and context-aware coherence cues at each decoding step.
AGMark adaptively determines the proportion of semantic-critical tokens using token entropy and evidence weight density for vocabulary partitioning.
AGMark embeds detectable signals while targeting preservation of visual-semantic fidelity and inference efficiency.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Attention-Guided Dynamic Watermarking as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AGMark outperforms conventional methods and substantially improves generation quality, with particularly strong visual-semantic fidelity gains in later generation stages.
The authors report at least 99.36% AUC detection performance and at least 88.61% AUC attack resilience.
The authors report that AGMark preserves inference efficiency while maintaining competitive detection performance and attack resilience.

narrative_sequence.summary: Watermarking is motivated by traceability and intellectual property protection for large vision-language models.
Existing approaches can disrupt visual grounding, rely on static estimates, ignore weight density, and introduce low-quality or irrelevant tokens.
AGMark dynamically identifies semantic-critical evidence and adaptively partitions the vocabulary using attention, coherence, entropy, and weight-density signals.
The authors report improved generation quality and visual-semantic fidelity, competitive detection and attack-resilience AUC, and preserved inference efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The framework adapts token protection to changing visual dependence during generation using attention, entropy, and evidence density.

interpretation.claim: When relevance changes across decoding steps, dynamic evidence allocation may reduce interference from indiscriminate protection.

application.claim: Adaptive protection policies could be considered for multimodal generation systems where semantic relevance varies over time.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach generalizes beyond the evaluated large vision-language model setting.

unknowns: Datasets, model architectures, baselines, and experimental protocols are not specified.
The attack settings and detection evaluation details are not specified.
The meaning of the reported later-generation visual-semantic gains is not quantified beyond the abstract.
